_comment: Fragment 42 — D-89: branch protection set, D-82 closed with residual, G72 to backlog. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-89 — Branch Protection Set; D-82 Closed With Its Residual
nodes.description: Main requires a pull request and a passing status check, so CI now runs before a merge rather than after a commit lands. Main only; the working branch stays ungated. Recorded as the Chief Editor's statement rather than a measurement, because gh is not installed on this machine and no token is present, so branch protection cannot be verified from here.
nodes.rationale: Stated as asserted rather than measured because writing it as though it had been checked is the exact defect this register keeps finding. The alternative would have been a claim with nothing behind it.

nodes.label: Three Layers of Gating, One Still Open
nodes.description: Local commits are gated by the commit-msg hook requiring a Lane-Crossing trailer. Merges to main are gated by pull request plus a required status check. Pushes to the working branch are gated by nothing, and no-verify bypasses the local hook.
nodes.rationale: The residual is deliberate for Phase 1, where Lane A commits frequently and a pull request per commit would be friction for no benefit. It stops being the right trade when Lane B starts, and that is the moment to revisit.

nodes.label: The Required Status Check Name Contains Two Middle Dots
nodes.description: The CI job is named Typecheck, Lint, Test separated by U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT characters rather than hyphens or bullets. GitHub matches a required status check by that exact string, so if it was typed by hand with any other character the protection is configured and never gates.
nodes.rationale: A guard that fails open, the same pattern as the TMPDIR marker in D-81. The recommended fix is to rename the job to an ASCII string, but .github/workflows is Lane C's under D-84, so it is specified and not applied.

nodes.label: The Merge Gate Enforces Six of Nine Checks
nodes.description: graph-coverage and docs-drift read gitignored .graphify, and source-sweep needs per-file history that a depth-1 checkout does not have. All three skip in CI, so a merge to main can pass while the graph is stale or a governing document has drifted. Local bun run check is the only place all nine run.
nodes.rationale: Stated so the merge gate is not overread. A control whose blind spots are unstated invites the belief that everything it does not report is fine.

nodes.label: The Fast-Forward Merge Guidance Is Withdrawn
nodes.description: Advice given earlier in the session, to switch to main and merge with ff-only then push, no longer works because the direct push is now blocked. The merge to main goes through a pull request instead. Main remains a strict ancestor at zero behind and ninety-two ahead, so the merge is conflict-free and merge=union still never fires.
nodes.rationale: The advice was never written into any document, so it is corrected in the register rather than left standing in conversation where it would be re-read as current.

nodes.label: G72 to Backlog; the Distribution Choice Is @sentropic/graphify
nodes.description: Graph-schema compatibility with upstream stays unverified and moves to backlog, with no work until a related issue surfaces. The distribution decision is settled and unchanged under D-51: the project runs @sentropic/graphify, an attributed downstream extension of Graphify-Labs/graphify, and nothing proposes a swap.
nodes.rationale: Not a live risk while D-51 stands. Command availability is already known from D-60; schema shape is the thing to verify first if a swap is ever reconsidered.
